guidelines: 0 — Missing or fundamentally wrong: no usable evidence that this criterion is met.
1 — Major deficiencies: substantial changes are needed to meet this criterion.
2 — Partially meets expectations: meaningful work, but important gaps remain.
3 — Mostly meets expectations: sound work with minor gaps or defects.
4 — Fully meets expectations: complete, convincing evidence with no material gaps.

axes.title: Behavioral correctness
axes.description: Does the submitted study implement the requested participant flow and behavior? Compare the task prompt with final code and check results.
anchors: 0: Required flow is absent or unusable.
2: Some required paths work, but important behavior is missing or incorrect.
4: All requested paths and behaviors are implemented and supported by evidence.

axes.title: Experimental validity
axes.description: Does the implementation preserve the experiment design, including treatments, assignment, incentives, measurements, and stored data where requested?
anchors: 0: The implementation invalidates the intended experiment or measurements.
2: The design is partly preserved, but consequential assignment, incentive, or data issues remain.
4: The requested design and data semantics are faithfully implemented.

axes.title: Exercise and verification
axes.description: Did the agent exercise the study and verify its work? Inspect agent logs, exercise scripts, and check results for actual execution and meaningful coverage.
anchors: 0: No meaningful verification was performed.
2: Some checks were run, but key paths or assertions were omitted.
4: Relevant paths and data were exercised, results checked, and failures addressed.

axes.title: Robustness
axes.description: Does the study handle relevant invalid input, repeated actions, and state transitions reliably? Consider edge cases within the requested scope.
anchors: 0: Ordinary input or interaction breaks the study or corrupts state.
2: The happy path works, but relevant edge cases remain fragile.
4: Relevant input and state edge cases are handled consistently.

axes.title: Conscript quality
axes.description: Is the code clear, maintainable, and idiomatic Conscript? Inspect study structure, state handling, and use of existing APIs.
anchors: 0: Code is incoherent or fundamentally misuses Conscript.
2: Code is understandable but has significant structural or API-use problems.
4: Code uses appropriate Conscript patterns and is clear and maintainable.

axes.title: Scope discipline
axes.description: Did the agent stay within the requested task and allowed files? Compare changed files with the prompt and outcome scope violations.
anchors: 0: Changes substantially violate the allowed scope or damage unrelated behavior.
2: Work is mostly relevant but includes unnecessary or out-of-scope changes.
4: Changes are focused on the task and respect all scope constraints.

axes.title: Handoff
axes.description: Does the final response accurately explain what was delivered, what was verified, and any limitations? Compare the agent summary with the saved evidence.
anchors: 0: The handoff is absent or materially misleading.
2: The summary is useful but omits important verification details or limitations.
4: The handoff is concise, accurate, and clearly reports verification and remaining limitations.

guidance: Read the task prompt and review the submitted files, outcome, and agent logs before scoring. Judge each axis independently against the task requirements. Passing automated checks alone does not establish a top score. Use notes to cite evidence and explain uncertainty; if you cannot assess an axis yet, abort and resume grading after review.
